pageCache.pageTitle: Headteacher's Welcome — South Ascot Village School
pageCache.text:
children have one go at their education, and one go at their childhood. So let’s make it count.
Welcome to the South Ascot Village School (SAVS) website, where you can find information about our fantastic, vibrant and inclusive school community. Here, you will find information about our mainstream classrooms, the enriching Forest School, and the Canopy - our specialist unit catering specifically for pupils with Autism.
We believe passionately in nurturing every individual and facilitating their sense of belonging and access to community, because Together we have strength.
Our school is built on care, inclusivity, and a shared commitment to nurturing the dreams, ambitions, and aspirations of all pupils, staff and families. Our school community is a special place where we value, respect, and support each other to thrive in a safe and caring environment. We celebrate diversity and foster high expectations, expert teaching, and continuous improvement to ensure every pupil achieves their full potential.
We are united by determination, creativity, and care—reflecting our shared vision and values embodied in our symbolic journey from curiosity to success. Together, we create a place where children love to learn, grow, and flourish.
We warmly invite you to explore our website and join us in supporting the dreams and ambitions of every member of the SAVS family.
J Corbitt, Headteacher

pageCache.pageTitle: Wraparound Care — South Ascot Village School
pageCache.text:
wraparound care
Before School Provision
Children attending South Ascot Village School from Reception to Year 6 are eligible to attend the Breakfast Club, subject to availability of places.
The club operates from 7.30am and pupils requiring breakfast must arrive by 8.15am. Children attending will be offered a breakfast, in line with the School Food Regulations, January 2015, which will include: fruit juice, milk or water; cereal; toast with butter/jam/honey/marmite; yoghurt; and, fresh fruit.
Bookings must be made before midnight the day before the booking date using the school's SCOPAY App. Bookings can be made up to a term in advance and places are allocated on a first come first basis.
Priority booking for some places will be given to families of pupils in receipt of Pupil Premium and the school is registered to accept childcare vouchers.
Breakfast Club prices are currently set at £7 per morning session of any length.
After School Provision
Children attending South Ascot Village School from Reception to Year 6 are eligible to attend the After School Club, subject to availability of places.
The club operates from 3.10 to either 4.30 for a short session or 5.30 for the long session. Children attending will be offered a sandwich or wrap, biscuit, fresh fruit, water or fruit juice.
Bookings must be made before midnight the day before using the school's SCOPAY App, and payment is due at the time of making the booking.
Priority booking for some places will be given to families of pupils in receipt of Pupil Premium and the school is registered to accept childcare vouchers.
After School Club prices are currently set at - £9 from 3.10pm - 4.30pm session and £14 from 3.10pm - 5.30pm

pageCache.pageTitle: Our Curriculum — South Ascot Village School
pageCache.text:
Our curriculum is thoughtfully designed to inspire curiousity, creativity and a lifelong love of learning.
Rooted in the national curriculum and enriched by our school’s unique vision and values, we provide a broad, balanced, and coherent learning journey that meets the diverse needs of our community. Through expert teaching and carefully sequenced knowledge, skills, and experiences, we ensure all pupils build strong foundations, make meaningful progress, and develop the confidence to succeed both in school and beyond.
Explore the SAVS Curriculum by Subject
English
Our English curriculum ignites curiosity, builds confident readers and writers, and develops critical thinkers. Through engaging texts, purposeful talk, phonics mastery and progressive grammar, pupils craft clear, creative writing and secure comprehension. Inclusive assessment and rich vocabulary teaching ensure every child makes measurable progress, ready to communicate with confidence and flourish across the wider curriculum and life beyond school.
Maths
Our maths curriculum is bold and ambitious, igniting curiosity and confidence. Using a mastery approach, it moves from concrete to pictorial to abstract, building deep understanding. Pupils tackle challenging problems, reason precisely and communicate clearly, with regular retrieval practice and thoughtful scaffolding that supports mastery.
See our latest Calculation & Vocabulary Curriculum by clicking here.
Wonder Week
Wonder Weeks incorporate cross-curricular learning in Art and Design, Design and Technology and Music (and more!) They draw on learning across all subjects. Linked to a school trip and whole-school showcase event every half-term for every pupil, Wonder Weeks are a time for the SAVS community to really comes to life.
Forest School
Our Forest School curriculum ignites curiosity and resilience by delivering weekly outdoor sessions that build practical skills, confidence and environmental stewardship. Led by trained Forest School practitioners, children explore woodland habitats, tool use, fire safety and seasonal crafts, developing teamwork, independence and a lifelong respect for nature.
Science
Our bold Science curriculum sparks curiosity and builds practical skills through hands‑on investigations, outdoor learning and real‑world problem solving. Pupils explore biology, chemistry and physics using enquiry, teamwork and clear scientific vocabulary, preparing them to question, experiment and confidently explain the world around them.
Humanities
Our Geography and History curriculum sparks curiosity and builds confident, enquiring minds. Pupils explore local to global places, map skills and human-environment links, while uncovering chronological stories, enquiry skills and diverse perspectives. Hands-on fieldwork, sources and ambitious vocabulary ensure learners think critically, make connections and become informed, courageous citizens.
Physical Education
Our PE curriculum inspires confident, healthy pupils through varied, inclusive physical activity. From fundamental movement and team sports to dance and outdoor education, lessons build skills, resilience and fair play. Progressive assessment ensures every child develops fitness, coordination and leadership, ready for lifelong active living and positive wellbeing.
Personal Development
Our Personal Development Curriculum is not limited to planned sequences and the specific learning intentions that are targeted through additional whole school, class and group activities. Our approach is in the belief that self-regulation, metacognition and mindset are key factors in a person’s ability to enjoy, plan and experience success.
Personal, Social, Health and Economic
Our PSHE curriculum empowers primary pupils with age-appropriate lessons on wellbeing, relationships, safety and citizenship. Through active, inclusive activities and clear values, children build resilience, emotional literacy and respectful behaviours, preparing them to make safe, healthy choices and contribute positively to school and wider community.
Religious Education
Our Religious Education curriculum inspires curiosity, respect and critical thinking. Pupils explore diverse beliefs, traditions and moral questions through age-appropriate enquiry, discussion and reflection. Lessons build knowledge, empathy and British values, encouraging pupils to appreciate difference, make thoughtful choices and engage confidently with the world around them.
Homework
Homework helps primary children consolidate classroom learning, build independent study habits and time management, and deepen understanding through gentle practice. Regular, short tasks strengthen confidence, parental engagement and school–home links while identifying gaps early. When well-planned and age-appropriate, homework supports progress, resilience and a positive attitude to lifelong learning.
Languages
Our French curriculum sparks curiosity and confidence through spoken and cultural learning. Children build vocabulary, pronunciation and conversation skills via songs, games and stories, progressing from simple greetings to short descriptions. Lessons foster curiosity about cultures, promote communication, cultural respect and a lifelong love of language.
